formation.text: Default to F1 formation (spread), not stack/block — tight formations are easy for enemy heroes to flank and disrupt with CC; F1's spread means CC only disables part of the formation while the majority keeps functioning. Exception: in narrow terrain that prevents enemy flanking, use F2 block formation to maximize damage concentration in the center.

mechanics.name: First-hit immunity ('blue bar')
mechanics.text: Indicated by a blue bar above the health bar. Recharges after 30 seconds out of combat. Blocks even crowd-control effects including hero ultimate abilities.

mechanics.name: Pike rotation (V)
mechanics.text: Press V to unlock pike rotation — lets all models rotate to face the nearest enemy when enemies concentrate on one side, so the whole formation can deal damage instead of only half (roughly doubling effective contact vs. a static spread).

mechanics.name: Instant brace, stability, and advance behavior
mechanics.text: Instant brace combo: press 1 to brace (normal animation), or 1 then V to skip the animation and have pikes drop instantly with brace effects (including CC) applied immediately. Stability (second stage) lets the unit move forward/backward while facing its orientation — the primary distance-control tool while braced. Brace applies crowd control; the advance order does NOT cancel brace status or its effects, but advancing adds no extra damage — ramming into enemies while braced (an Imperial Pike playstyle) is explicitly called 'the worst thing you can do while controlling this unit.' Advance marches infinitely until reactivated or stopped with V.

mechanics.name: Second ability ('Area's Fury' per transcript / 'Ares' Flurry' per Amya)
mechanics.text: Damage-dealing ability: forcefully overextends the unit forward into closer melee range; cancels brace status for its duration; deals significant damage in return. Because of the forced overextension, the guide recommends advancing backwards afterward (optional but recommended) to regain safe distance.

scenarios.label: Engagement and reach control
scenarios.text: Follow the front line, instant-brace at safe distance (accounting for enemy long pikemen), advance forward once in range, stop with V. If the team pushes through, keep following + stopping with V once in reach; if the team is losing ground, advance backward to hold distance while still dealing damage. Explicit tip: minimize command-to-execution delay — 'the longer you take to adjust your distance the easier your enemies can adapt to your range.'

scenarios.label: Full engagement and distance control
scenarios.text: Same base pattern plus a layer — follow the front line, brace at safe distance, V to skip animation, advance until in reach, stop with V, use the second ability (forces overextension), then immediately advance backward to regain safe distance and resume following the front line. Real-battle walkthrough includes a 'fake a huge retreat' bait-and-re-engage moment and a formation reform after over-spreading.

scenarios.label: Defense and disengagement/regrouping
scenarios.text: Mirror pattern focused on advancing backward to prevent enemies reaching the unit, especially with a broken front line: brace → wait for impact → readjust distance if needed → V → second ability (forces forward move) → immediately advance backward → V again once far enough. Forced dispersal (enemy units or hero CC) is corrected by advancing backward while looking for regroup opportunities, then X (regroup on a chosen location) + re-brace.

scenarios.label: Long-range hero engagement and regrouping
scenarios.text: Judge whether it's safe to exit formation (e.g., a hero diving to disrupt while their unit is still far away, or the player overextending) → quick X then V to melt the nearest target with basic attacks → if the hero survives, regroup ASAP and re-brace even accepting some losses or an imperfect reform.

quotes.text: Master the double C brace, you get 3-4x area coverage with minimal DPS loss.
